content:
Hello, I'm wondering what the current situation is for formalisation of Random Matrix Theory, in mathlib, tau ceti or other places? Specifically, the material covered by the three books, 1. "An Introduction to Random Matrices", Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, 2. "Topics in Random Matrix Theory", Tao, 3. "A first course in Random Matrix Theory", Potters and Bouchaud.
Thanks in advance for any information!

Here's some recent discussion:

#maths > Formalizing Probabilistic Arguments
#maths > what's the status of random matrix theory? (last traffic a year ago)
#mathlib4 > Why does mathlib have matrices? @ 💬
#new members > Introduction @ 💬
#new members > Intro: David Buzinski @ 💬

It would be great to makes some more progress here!

I wrote up a preliminary roadmap for Tau Ceti for random matrix theory: TauCetiRoadmap#397. I might ping a few people to see if anyone is interested either in reviewing, or just describing things they would like to see done in Tau Ceti, or not done because they are actively working on it elsewhere.

@David Ledvinka @Fred Rajasekaran @Rémy Degenne @Yuanhe Zhang @Edward van de Meent @Peter Pfaffelhuber @Etienne Marion

(Please don't feel at all pressured to read the :robot: written roadmap at TauCetiRoadmap#397. Non-:robot: mediated conversation here about plans for random matrices theory is great too!)

Yes, I'd be happy to review/help design a roadmap. I remember one challenging thing when I was working on RMT was getting a good definition of an empirical measure that works well with downstream measurability lemmas, so maybe this could be good to figure out first. Also the method of moments proofs relied on counting walks on graphs which was hard to do with the Mathlib API at the time, but not it might be easier now with LLMS.

In terms of content it would be nice to have the matrix concentration inequalities (eg from Joel Tropp or van Handel's recent work), since they're pretty applicable in many different contexts.

Hi @Kim Morrison thanks very much for all that, very useful!

@Fred Rajasekaran actually I had previously seen your work on the semicircle law
https://fredraj3.github.io/SemicircleLaw/
I should have mentioned that.
Yes agree that Tropp + van Handel, matrix concentration inequalities would be a good thing to aim for.
fwiw I saw both of them speak at ICM.
